claims.text: Grants are available from the Morris Fund.
Grant amounts range from £500 to £5,000.
Grants are for the conservation of decorative or non-structural interior features.
Eligible features must be in UK places of worship.
Eligible features must be pre-1896.
Work must follow SPAB principles.
There are two application rounds per year.

records.justification: The agent's text accurately reflects the grant amount, purpose, and broad eligibility criteria as described in the provided page text.

claims.text: The Society makes annual project grants of £500 to £5,000.
The grants support research into the human past through its material culture or material remains.
There are no period, geographic, or disciplinary restrictions for these grants.

Applications are encouraged across archaeology, art history, architectural and buildings history, studies of material culture items and assemblages (including books and manuscripts), the history of collecting and collections, and the development of intellectual enquiry into the human past through its material remains.

records.justification: The agent's text captures several eligibility and amount claims but omits all claims related to the specific type of institution, the nature of the items to be conserved, and the requirement for a professional director.

claims.text: Applications must be on behalf of a church, chapel, or other place of worship in the United Kingdom.
Funds are available for the conservation of decorative or non-structural interior features.
Eligible features include stained glass, sculpture, furniture, monuments/tombs, and wall paintings.
The object to be conserved must have been made no later than 1896.
References are not required for applications.
A professional architect or established conservator must direct the work.
Turret clocks and organs are not grant-aided.
Applications for a clock or organ case of significant contribution or antiquarian interest may exceptionally be considered.
Applications must be from the project director or principal investigator.
Awards will not be made for work contributing to an undergraduate or postgraduate degree.
Retrospective applications will not be considered.
Eligible project costs include travel & subsistence for project team members.
Eligible project costs include the costs of specialist or scientific investigation.
Eligible project costs include the costs of technical services such as imaging and illustration, where these have to be commissioned.
Eligible project costs include the hire of plant and site accommodation.
Eligible project costs include materials and consumables.
Eligible project costs include the hire of specialist equipment to which the applicant cannot reasonably be expected to have access.
Personal remuneration is not an eligible cost.
Salaries of staff holding current appointments are not eligible costs.
Institutional overheads are not eligible costs.
Internal hire charges within the applicant’s institution or between project partners are not eligible costs.
Publication subventions and publication grants (including costs of digital dissemination) are not eligible costs.
Contingency estimates are not eligible costs.

records.justification: All claims made in the agent's text regarding eligibility and eligible/ineligible project costs are directly supported by the provided page text.
